q: Materials which have an electrical resistance that lies between the high resistance values of insulators and the low resistance values of metals are called ____.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. Materials which have an electrical resistance that lies between the high resistance values of insulators and the low resistance values of metals are called semiconductors.

q: For example, ____ and silicon are commonly used semiconductors.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. For example, germanium and silicon are commonly used semiconductors.

q: Gallium arsenide(GaAs) and ____ are used as semiconductors.
e: Ge and Si are elemental semiconductors. GaAs and CdTe are compound semiconductors. Gallium arsenide(GaAs) and Cadmium Telluride(CdTe) are used as semiconductors.

q: They are ____ semiconductors.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. They are compound semiconductors.

q: In metals, ____ are the charge carriers.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. In metals, electrons are the charge carriers.

q: In the case of semiconductors, both electrons and ____ are the charge carriers.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. In the case of semiconductors, both electrons and positive holes are the charge carriers.

q: A vacancy which is left by an electron in the semiconductor atom is called a ____.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. A vacancy which is left by an electron in the semiconductor atom is called a positive hole.

q: When the potential is applied to two ends of a semiconductor, electrons moves from lower potential to higher one, while the ____ move in the opposite direction.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. When the potential is applied to two ends of a semiconductor, electrons moves from lower potential to higher one, while the positive holes move in the opposite direction.

q: This means that the current flows due to the movement of ____ in the case of semiconductors.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. This means that the current flows due to the movement of electrons and holes in the case of semiconductors.

q: Pure semiconductors have ____ of electrons, and positive holes.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. Pure semiconductors have equal numbers of electrons, and positive holes.

q: Since these are relatively few in number at normal temperature, pure semiconductors have ____.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. Since these are relatively few in number at normal temperature, pure semiconductors have poor conductivity.

q: When a few ____ are added to the pure semiconductor, its conductivity increases.
e: A little donor or acceptor impurity, doping, makes n-type or p-type material and raises conductivity. When a few impurity atoms are added to the pure semiconductor, its conductivity increases.

q: Arsenic, aluminium and ____ atoms are used as impurity atoms.
e: A little donor or acceptor impurity, doping, makes n-type or p-type material and raises conductivity. Arsenic, aluminium and indium atoms are used as impurity atoms.

q: As a result, ____ types of semiconductor are obtained.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. As a result, two types of semiconductor are obtained.

q: When arsenic atoms having ____ valence electrons are added to the pure semiconductor (Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. When arsenic atoms having five valence electrons are added to the pure semiconductor (Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.

q: Since the number of electrons is greater than that of positive holes in this impure semiconductor it is called an ____.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. Since the number of electrons is greater than that of positive holes in this impure semiconductor it is called an n-type semiconductor.

q: In the n-type semiconductor ____ are the majority charge carriers of electric current.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. In the n-type semiconductor electrons are the majority charge carriers of electric current.

q: When indium atoms having ____ valence electrons are added to pure semiconductor(Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.
e: A group-V atom (five valence electrons) donates an electron. A group-III atom (three valence electrons) accepts one and leaves a hole. When indium atoms having three valence electrons are added to pure semiconductor(Ge, Si) atoms having four valence electrons, the conductivity of pure semiconductor increases.

q: Since the number of positive holes is greater than that of electrons in this impure semiconductor it is called a ____.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. Since the number of positive holes is greater than that of electrons in this impure semiconductor it is called a p-type semiconductor.

q: Thus in a p-type semiconductor ____ are the majority charge carriers of electric current.
e: A group-III acceptor makes a p-type semiconductor. Holes are the majority carriers. Thus in a p-type semiconductor positive holes are the majority charge carriers of electric current.

q: A boundary or junction is formed between p-type and n-type semiconductors by semiconductor device fabrication process, and this junction is called a ____.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. A boundary or junction is formed between p-type and n-type semiconductors by semiconductor device fabrication process, and this junction is called a p-n junction.

q: A device which consists of a p-n junction is called a ____.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. A device which consists of a p-n junction is called a p-n junction diode.

q: When a battery is joined with its negative terminal to the p-type and its positive terminal to the n-type, only a very small current flows through the p-n junction diode, and it is said to be ____.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. When a battery is joined with its negative terminal to the p-type and its positive terminal to the n-type, only a very small current flows through the p-n junction diode, and it is said to be reverse-biased.

q: It means that the current flows in ____ only from the anode to the cathode in a vacuum diode and from p to n in a p-n junction diode.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. It means that the current flows in one direction only from the anode to the cathode in a vacuum diode and from p to n in a p-n junction diode.

q: Anode and cathode of a p-n junction, not in connection with a battery, are not at the same electric potential because there is initially a ____ across the junction.
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Anode and cathode of a p-n junction, not in connection with a battery, are not at the same electric potential because there is initially a potential difference across the junction.

q: A rectifier is a device which converts an alternating current (AC) into a unidirectional current or a ____.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. A rectifier is a device which converts an alternating current (AC) into a unidirectional current or a direct current (DC).

q: Diodes can be used as rectifiers because the current flows in ____ only from anode to cathode.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. Diodes can be used as rectifiers because the current flows in one direction only from anode to cathode.

q: The diagram shown in Figure 11.5 (a) is that of a ____.
e: The diagram shown in Figure 11.5 (a) is that of a half-wave rectifier. Half-wave rectifier is what this statement is using.

q: There is only ____ diode in the half-wave rectifier circuit.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. There is only one diode in the half-wave rectifier circuit.

q: As the current I flows in the diode for every first half of the cycle of AC, this device acts as a ____.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. As the current I flows in the diode for every first half of the cycle of AC, this device acts as a half-wave rectifier.

q: The circuit diagram shown in Figure 11.6(a) is that of a ____.
e: The circuit diagram shown in Figure 11.6(a) is that of a full-wave rectifier. Full-wave rectifier is what this statement is using.

q: The full-wave rectifier circuit consists of ____ diodes.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. The full-wave rectifier circuit consists of two diodes.

q: Since D1 and D2 operate ____ for one cycle of an AC voltage, current always flows through the resistor R.
e: Since D1 and D2 operate alternately for one cycle of an AC voltage, current always flows through the resistor R. Alternately is what this statement is using. Alternately is what this sentence is naming.

q: As the current flows through R for both half-cycle of the AC voltage, this device is called a ____.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. As the current flows through R for both half-cycle of the AC voltage, this device is called a full-wave rectifier.

q: The principal application of a rectifier is to convert ____.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. The principal application of a rectifier is to convert AC to DC.

q: Most of the electronic devices require ____ for their operation.
e: Most of the electronic devices require DC power for their operation. Dc power is what this statement is using.

q: A transistor is a semiconductor device which works as an ____.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. A transistor is a semiconductor device which works as an amplifier.

q: In ____, three American physicists Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain invented the transistor.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In 1949, three American physicists Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain invented the transistor.

q: A transistor is made of ____ layers of p- and n-semiconductors.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. A transistor is made of three layers of p- and n-semiconductors.

q: There are two common kinds of transistors called the ____ transistors.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. There are two common kinds of transistors called the pnp and npn transistors.

q: In a pnp transistor a thin layer of ____ is sandwiched between two layers of p-semiconductors.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In a pnp transistor a thin layer of n-semiconductor is sandwiched between two layers of p-semiconductors.

q: In an npn transistor a thin layer of ____ is sandwiched between two layers of n-semiconductors.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In an npn transistor a thin layer of p-semiconductor is sandwiched between two layers of n-semiconductors.

q: An electrode is attached to each layer and hence there are three electrodes; the ____, the collector (C) and the base (B) in a transistor.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. An electrode is attached to each layer and hence there are three electrodes; the emitter(E), the collector (C) and the base (B) in a transistor.

q: Transistors do not ____ with time, whereas vacuum tubes do.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Transistors do not deteriorate with time, whereas vacuum tubes do.

q: Transistors are physically much more ____ than vacuum tubes.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Transistors are physically much more robust than vacuum tubes.

q: Transistors waste much less ____ than vacuum tubes.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Transistors waste much less electrical power than vacuum tubes.

q: There is no ____ after switching on a transistor.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. There is no warm-up period after switching on a transistor.

q: Transistors are very much ____ than vacuum tubes but they perform a similar function.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Transistors are very much smaller than vacuum tubes but they perform a similar function.

q: In a transistor biasing circuit, a current ____ flows in the collector circuit.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In a transistor biasing circuit, a current I_C flows in the collector circuit.

q: The remainder of positive holes flows into the base so that the current ____ is obtained.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. The remainder of positive holes flows into the base so that the current I_B is obtained.

q: If $I_E$ is a current which flows across the emitter, then ____.
e: If I_E is a current which flows across the emitter, then I_E = I_C + I_B. Leave the relation as I_E = I_C + I_B.

q: However, the base is so thin that $I_B \sim 0.02 I_E$ and ____.
e: However, the base is so thin that I_B sim 0.02 I_E and I_C sim 0.98 I_E. I_c sim 0.98 i_e is what this statement is using.

q: Therefore, the small base current $I_B$ can control a very large ____.
e: Therefore, the small base current I_B can control a very large collector current. Collector current is what this statement is using.

q: Because of this property a transistor can be regarded as a ____.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Because of this property a transistor can be regarded as a current amplifier.

q: The resistance of forward-biased emitter junction is ____ and that of reverse-biased collector junction is large.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The resistance of forward-biased emitter junction is small and that of reverse-biased collector junction is large.

q: Since the electrical power is ____, the power in the emitter side is small whereas the power in the collector side is large.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Since the electrical power is I²R, the power in the emitter side is small whereas the power in the collector side is large.

q: Therefore, the transistor can be regarded as a ____.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Therefore, the transistor can be regarded as a power amplifier.

q: Because the thickness of the base is about ____ and the base layer of a transistor is thinner than other two layers, the value of base current $I_B$ is very small.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Because the thickness of the base is about 10^-3 cm and the base layer of a transistor is thinner than other two layers, the value of base current I_B is very small.

q: An arrangement whereby connections of electronic components such as resistors, capacitors and transistors are made is called an ____.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. An arrangement whereby connections of electronic components such as resistors, capacitors and transistors are made is called an electronic circuit.

q: The three groups of the electronic circuit are (i) vacuum tube circuit (ii) transistor circuit and (iii) ____.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. The three groups of the electronic circuit are (i) vacuum tube circuit (ii) transistor circuit and (iii) integrated circuit(IC).

q: In the integrated circuit, all the electronic components and connections required for an electronic circuit are all made on ____.
e: In the integrated circuit, all the electronic components and connections required for an electronic circuit are all made on one single semiconductor crystal. One single semiconductor crystal is what this statement is using.

q: Electronic circuits can be divided into two categories, ____.
e: Electronic circuits can be divided into two categories, analog and digital. Analog and digital is what this statement is using.

q: Analog electronics involves quantities with ____, and digital electronics involves quantities with discrete values.
e: Analog electronics involves quantities with continuous values, and digital electronics involves quantities with discrete values. Continuous values is what this statement is using.

q: Digital electronics involves circuits and systems in which there are only ____ possible states.
e: Digital electronics involves circuits and systems in which there are only two possible states. Two is what this statement is using.

q: These states are represented by two different voltage levels: a ____ and a LOW (logic 0).
e: These states are represented by two different voltage levels: a HIGH (logic 1) and a LOW (logic 0). High (logic 1) is what this statement is using.

q: In digital systems such as computers, combinations of the two states, called ____, are used to represent numbers, symbols, alphabetic characters, and other types of information.
e: In digital systems such as computers, combinations of the two states, called codes, are used to represent numbers, symbols, alphabetic characters, and other types of information. The name used here is codes.

q: The ____ is a way to represent or express numbers.
e: The number system is a way to represent or express numbers. Number system is what this statement is using.

q: There are various types of number systems such as the ____ and the binary numbers system.
e: There are various types of number systems such as the decimal numbers system and the binary numbers system. Decimal numbers system is what this statement is using.

q: In the decimal number system, the digits ____ represents numbers.
e: In the decimal number system, the digits 0 to 9 represents numbers. 0 to 9 is what this statement is using.

q: As it uses 10 digits to represent a number, it is also called the ____.
e: As it uses 10 digits to represent a number, it is also called the base 10. The name used here is base 10.

q: The position of each digit in a decimal number is positive powers of ten that increase from right to left, beginning with ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The position of each digit in a decimal number is positive powers of ten that increase from right to left, beginning with 10^0=1.

q: The binary number is another way to represent quantities and it has only ____.
e: The binary number is another way to represent quantities and it has only two digits. Two digits is what this statement is using.

q: A computer can understand only the ____ state of a switch.
e: A computer can understand only the "on" and "off" state of a switch. "on" and "off" is what this statement is using.

q: These two states are represented by ____.
e: These two states are represented by 1 and 0. 1 and 0 is what this statement is using.

q: A binary number is a ____.
e: A binary number is a weighted number. Weighted number is what this statement is using.

q: The right-most bit is the ____ in a binary whole number and its weight is $2^0 = 1$.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. The right-most bit is the LSB (least significant bit) in a binary whole number and its weight is 2^0 = 1.

q: The weight increases from right to left by a ____ for each bit.
e: The weight increases from right to left by a power of two for each bit. Power of two is what this statement is using.

q: The left-most bit is the ____; its weight depends on the size of the binary number.
e: The left-most bit is the MSB (most significant bit); its weight depends on the size of the binary number. Msb (most significant bit) is what this statement is using.

q: The term 'bit' is abbreviation of the words ____.
e: The term 'bit' is abbreviation of the words 'binary' and 'digit'. 'binary' and 'digit' is what this statement is using.

q: A bit is the ____ of memory or instruction that can be given or stored on a computer.
e: A bit is the smallest unit of memory or instruction that can be given or stored on a computer. Smallest unit is what this statement is using.

q: A bit is either a ____.
e: A bit is either a 0 or a 1. 0 or a 1 is what this statement is using.

q: A group of ____ like 10100000 is a byte.
e: A group of 8 bits like 10100000 is a byte. 8 bits is what this statement is using.

q: ____ form a megabyte (MB).
e: 1024 kilobytes (kB) form a megabyte (MB). 1024 kilobytes (kb) is what this statement is using.

q: ____ form one gigabyte(GB).
e: 1024 megabytes form one gigabyte(GB). 1024 megabytes is what this statement is using.

q: ____ form one terabyte.
e: 1024 gigabytes form one terabyte. 1024 gigabytes is what this statement is using.

q: A ____ is an electronic device which takes an information from the environment, makes a decision based on that information and then gives out the result.
e: A logic gate is an electronic device which takes an information from the environment, makes a decision based on that information and then gives out the result. Logic gate is what this statement is using.

q: Logic gates can be built up using ____ of resistors, diodes and transistors.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. Logic gates can be built up using discrete components of resistors, diodes and transistors.

q: However, it is more convenient to use small ____.
e: However, it is more convenient to use small integrated circuits (ICs). Integrated circuits (ics) is what this statement is using.

q: The five common logic gates are ____ gates.
c: AND, OR, NAND, NOR and NOT (inverter)
e: The five common logic gates are AND, OR, NAND, NOR and NOT (inverter) gates. And, or, nand, nor and not (inverter) is what this statement is using.

q: Logic gate can have two or more inputs but only ____.
e: Logic gate can have two or more inputs but only one output. One output is what this statement is using.

q: But, NOT gate has only ____.
e: But, NOT gate has only one input. One input is what this statement is using.

q: For a 2-input AND gate, output X is HIGH only when inputs A and B are ____.
e: For a 2-input AND gate, output X is HIGH only when inputs A and B are HIGH. High is what this statement is using.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input AND gate is ____.
e: The Boolean expression for a 2-input AND gate is X=AB. Leave the relation as X=AB.

q: For a 2-input OR gate, output X is LOW only when both A and B are ____.
e: For a 2-input OR gate, output X is LOW only when both A and B are LOW. Low is what this statement is using.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input OR gate is ____.
e: The Boolean expression for a 2-input OR gate is X=A+B. Leave the relation as X=A+B. X=a+b is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: For a 2-input NAND gate, output X is LOW only when inputs A and B are ____.
e: For a 2-input NAND gate, output X is LOW only when inputs A and B are HIGH. High is what this statement is using.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NAND gate is ____.
e: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NAND gate is X=AB. Leave the relation as X=AB.

q: For a 2-input NOR gate, output X is HIGH only when both A and B are ____.
e: For a 2-input NOR gate, output X is HIGH only when both A and B are LOW. Low is what this statement is using.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NOR gate is ____.
e: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NOR gate is X=A+B. Leave the relation as X=A+B. X=a+b is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: The NAND gate and NOR gate are popular logic gates because they can be used as ____, that is, they alone can be used in combination to perform the functions of any other types of gates.
e: The NAND gate and NOR gate are popular logic gates because they can be used as universal gates, that is, they alone can be used in combination to perform the functions of any other types of gates. Universal gates is what this statement is using.

q: The inverter (NOT gate) performs the operation called ____.
e: The inverter (NOT gate) performs the operation called inversion. The name used here is inversion.

q: The inverter changes one logic level to the ____.
e: The inverter changes one logic level to the opposite level. Opposite level is what this statement is using.

q: When a LOW level is applied to its input, a ____ will appear on its output.
e: When a LOW level is applied to its input, a HIGH level will appear on its output. High level is what this statement is using.

q: The Boolean expression for a NOT gate is ____.
e: The Boolean expression for a NOT gate is X=A. Leave the relation as X=A. X=a is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.
